facts.statement: Niobrarasaurus coleii is the only known species in the extinct genus Niobrarasaurus.
facts.quote: Niobrarasaurus coleii es la única especie conocida del género extinto Niobrarasaurus

facts.statement: Niobrarasaurus was an armored dinosaur approximately 5 meters long, 1.8 meters high, and weighing between 227 and 453 kilograms.
facts.quote: Fue un dinosaurio acorazado de alrededor de 5 metros de largo, 1,8 de alto y un peso alrededor de 227 a 453 kilogramos

facts.statement: A higher estimate by Paul suggests the dinosaur reached 6.5 meters in length and 4 tons in weight.
facts.quote: Paul dio una estimación más alta de 6,5 metros y 4 toneladas

facts.statement: Niobrarasaurus was a nodosaurid ankylosaurian that lacked the club on its tail.
facts.quote: Niobrarasaurus era un Nodosauridae, un anquilosauriano sin la porra en la cola

facts.statement: The dinosaur lived at the end of the Cretaceous period, between 87 and 83 million years ago, during the Coniacian and Santonian stages.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 87 y 83 millones de años, entre el Coniaciense y el Santoniense

facts.statement: The fossil record indicates a time range from the Coniacian to Santonian stages, between 89.8 and 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Coniacian to Santonian (89.8 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils of Niobrarasaurus were found in the Smoky Hill Chalk Member of the Niobrara Formation in western Kansas.
facts.quote: Its fossils were found in the Smoky Hill Chalk Member of the Niobrara Formation, in western Kansas

facts.statement: Fossils were discovered in the Smoky Hill Chalk Member of the Niobrara Formation in western Kansas.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles fueron encontrados en el Miembro Smoky Hill Chalk de la Formación Niobrara, en Kansas occidental

facts.statement: The habitat was near the middle of the Western Interior Seaway during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: which would have been near the middle of the Western Interior Seaway during the Late Cretaceous

facts.statement: The remains were discovered in Gove County, about 11 miles south of Hackberry, Kansas, approximately 195 feet above the base of the Niobrara Formation.
facts.quote: It was discovered in Gove County, around 11 mi south of Hackberry, Kansas, around 195 ft above the base of the Niobrara Formation within the Smoky Hill Chalk Member

facts.statement: In 2002, the type specimen was transferred to the Sternberg Museum of Natural History in Hays, Kansas.
facts.quote: En 2002 el espécimen tipo fue transferido al Museo de Historia Natural de Sternberg, Hays, Kansas

facts.statement: Niobrarasaurus is classified within the family Nodosauridae.
The genus authority is Carpenter et al., 1995.
The genus name Niobrarasaurus was chosen to honor the Niobrara Formation where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: Carpenter and colleagues named the new genus Niobrarasaurus for the species, with the genus named after the Niobrara Formation it was found in

facts.statement: The description is based on a good skeleton with additional remains, including juvenile leg bones showing possible shark bite marks.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Hierosaurus coleii should be considered a distinct genus or a synonym of Nodosaurus, leading to its reclassification as Niobrarasaurus.
